title: Microrelease Stability & Stakeholder Activation Lab Journal
body:
Purpose: quick lab-journal for running very small, high-frequency microreleases (0.1%–5%) where stability signals, stakeholder activation, and human-in-loop choreography matter more than feature metrics. This is a working scratchpad — not canonical.

Audience: release stewards, SRE oncall, product owners, solutions eng for early customers.

Short summary: we ran three microreleases in Jan 2025 (alpha, beta, gamma) each targeting a different traffic slice and each instrumented with the same minimal telemetry set. Goals were: validate fallback latency profile, catch regressions vs eval prompt-set, and exercise the stakeholder notification choreography.

High-level lifecycle (microrelease):
- Preflight (T-48h): smoke tests (local canary runner), confirm synthetic replay script, stakeholder pre-commit (Slack stub).
- Pre-activation (T-2h): deploy to shadow pool, run 1k synthetic requests, confirm tail latency and token cost.
- Activation (T0): route X% traffic using staged-bucket allocator with bucketing by region and tier.
- Observation (T0+0–60m): continuous signal sampling. Decision at T+60 (extend/hold/rollback).
- Ramp / Hold: incremental increase if signals stable; immediate rollback on hard-failure thresholds.

Minimum telemetry (keep small for microreleases):
- P50, P90, P99 latency (inference and end-to-end)
- Tokens per request and token-cost delta vs baseline
- Error rate by error class (model-timeout, decode-error, input-parse)
- Output quality regression score (eval prompt-set bucketed by intent) — pass/fail on per-sample thresholds
- Session-level divergence: fraction of highest-prob failure cases flagged by safety heuristics

Gating thresholds (starter):
- Latency: P99 > baseline_P99 * 1.6 -> immediate rollback
- Error rate: absolute > 0.5% OR 3x baseline -> rollback
- Regression score: >5% of eval bucket samples drop > threshold -> hold and investigate
- Customer-x SLA hits: any customer impacted flag -> immediate manual rollback

Stakeholder activation choreography (practical):
- Owner (product steward) posts preflight note in #release-alerts 48h before. Include quick checklist link and runbook anchor.
- SRE oncall assigned to watch P99 and error rate for first 60m. Pager if threshold crossed.
- Solutions Eng (customer-facing) watches top-10 customer cohorts; prepared to trigger opt-out flag per-customer.
- Observability lead runs quick manual checks at 10m and 30m marks (sample outputs).
- Exec/PM sync only if public-facing or >0.5% user impact.

Sample tiny-run allocation strategy:
- Start: 0.25% global, split across region-weighted micro-slices (us-east-1: 0.12%, eu-west-1: 0.10%, ap-south: 0.03%).
- Flow: if all signals green at 30m, double allocation; repeat until target max or 2% cap reached.
- Maintain per-customer opt-out table and prefer stateless slices (no long-tail customers) to avoid stateful contamination.

Synthetic traffic recipe (fast smoke):
- 600 requests / region over 15m using replay harness seeded with recent user prompts (anonymized).
- Inject malformed inputs at 1% to surface parser regressions.
- Ensure diversity: short/long sequence, heavy-kv-cache hits, function-calling paths.

Runbook snippet (quick):
- If P99 spikes: check infra (GPU queue depth), switch to fallback model variant (quantized lower-latency) while triage.
- If errors increase: capture 200 sample logs, tag with cohort and stacktrace, notify dev owning model handler.
- If output regressions: pause traffic, snapshot rollout state, run offline eval against golden prompt-set; produce regression diff and escalate.

Escalation contacts (first-responder):
- SRE oncall: Miguel Torres
- Product steward: Asha Patel
- Observability: Emily Chen
- Customer engagement: Benji Rao

Lessons from Jan runs:
- Synthetic diversity matters — single-seed replays masked failure modes in apac region where sequence lengths differ.
- Token-cost delta is a leading indicator for perf regressions when quantization thresholds change.
- Human-in-loop checks at 10m caught a subtle hallucination for a high-value intent that automated eval missed. Keep 10m sample step.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define safe default for per-customer opt-out latency budget (Benji to propose by 2025-02-07).
- Can we automate 10m sample-output snapshots and route them to a small human review pool? (experiment: review-bot + ML classifier).
- Integrate rollback actuator with GitHub PR so rollbacks create a traceable revert PR automatically.

Next steps (short):
- Formalize the tiny-run allocation policy and ship tiny-run allocator into prod (owner: platform-engineering, ticket ROLL-824).
- Build a simple Slack cadence template for preflight / 10m / 30m / postmortem automated posts (observability team).
- Run two synthetic-only rehearsals (no live traffic) and capture baseline signal distributions for each region.

Notes to self: keep telemetry minimal for microreleases — too many signals adds noise and slow decision loops. Emphasize fast human checks + a tight three-signal rule (P99, error-rate, regression-score).
